routes.label: Take reciprocals to obtain linear relations
Express y and z in terms of x

question: If \(\dfrac{xy}{x+y}=a,\) \(\dfrac{xz}{x+z}=b,\) and \(\dfrac{yz}{y+z}=c,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) are other than zero, then \(x\) equals:
solution:
The numerators are products and the denominators are sums, so taking reciprocals will separate the variables. The original fractions must be defined. Since \(a,b,c\ne0\), their numerators are nonzero, which implies \(x,y,z\ne0\). Thus all the following reciprocals are valid:
\[
\frac1a=\frac1x+\frac1y,
\qquad
\frac1b=\frac1x+\frac1z,
\]
\[
\frac1c=\frac1y+\frac1z.
\]
These equations are linear in \(1/x,1/y,1/z\). Adding the first two and subtracting the third cancels the unwanted terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac2x
&=\frac1a+\frac1b-\frac1c\\
&=\frac{bc+ac-ab}{abc}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(abc\ne0\) and \(2/x\ne0\), the numerator \(ac+bc-ab\) is also nonzero. Multiplying by the nonzero denominators and solving gives
\[
x=\frac{2abc}{ac+bc-ab},
\]
which is choice E. This conclusion applies whenever the original defined equations have a solution.

solutionMethods.explanation:
We can eliminate \(y\) and \(z\) by solving the first two equations for them. Assume throughout that the original fractions are defined. Their nonzero values \(a,b,c\) imply \(x,y,z\ne0\).

Clearing the first denominator gives
\[
xy=a(x+y),\qquad y(x-a)=ax.
\]
Here \(x\ne a\): otherwise this equation would give \(0=a^2\), contrary to \(a\ne0\). Similarly, \(x\ne b\). Therefore
\[
y=\frac{ax}{x-a},\qquad z=\frac{bx}{x-b}.
\]
Adding these expressions gives
\[
y+z=\frac{x((a+b)x-2ab)}{(x-a)(x-b)}.
\]
Since \(y+z\ne0\), the factor \((a+b)x-2ab\) is nonzero. We may now substitute into the third equation and cancel the nonzero common factors:
\[
c=\frac{yz}{y+z}=\frac{abx}{(a+b)x-2ab}.
\]
Clearing this denominator and collecting the terms containing \(x\) yields
\[
(ac+bc-ab)x=2abc.
\]
The right side is nonzero, so \(ac+bc-ab\ne0\). Hence
\[
x=\frac{2abc}{ac+bc-ab},
\]
choice E, for every solution of the original defined equations.
solutionMethods.label: Express y and z in terms of x
